previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with epigastric and left upper quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, and constipation following recent discharge for secretin-induced pancreatitis. Initial concern for recurrent pancreatitis was tempered by only mildly elevated lipase and a soft, non-tender abdomen. Imaging revealed significant stool burden, and symptoms improved markedly after bowel regimen with polyethylene glycol and senna. Pain resolved, oral intake was advanced successfully, and labs stabilized. The patient was discharged home in stable condition with a soft diet, reduced pancreatic enzyme supplementation, and instructions for pain and constipation management. Follow-up was arranged with gastroenterology and primary care.

Brief Hospital Course:
This is a ___ year old female with pancreatitis and pancreatic 
cyst. She went to the OR on ___ for: 
1. Distal Pancreatectomy with splenectomy.
2. Enterectomy and primary closure with a small intestinal full 
thickness biopsy.

She did well post-operatively and followed a modified ""Whipple"" 
pathway.
Pain: She had a PCA for pain control. She was transitioned to 
oral pain medications once tolerating a diet. She required 
higher than usual doses of medication to control her pain.

GI/ABD: She was NPO, with a NGT and IVF. The NGT, was removed on 
POD 1. Her diet was slowly advanced as she had return of bowel 
function. She was tolerating clears liquids by POD4. On POD 5, a 
JP Amylase was measured and was 117. The drain was subsequently 
removed the next day.
Her abdomen was soft, nondistended and the incision with 
subcuticular suture was C/D/I. The patient was discharged with 
steri strips in place. JP drain was removed on POD #5. She was 
tolerating regular food and reported +flatus and +BM prior to 
discharge.

Post-op Tachycardia/Hypotension: She has a history of postural 
orthostatic hypotension/tachycardic syndrome. She was monitored 
closely and she was asymptomatic during her hospitalization. All 
of her home medications were restarted. 
 
Medications on Admission:
amitriptyline 50 qhs, fludrocortisone 0.1"

HISTORY:  Status post distal pancreatectomy and splenectomy, to evaluate for
central catheter.

FINDINGS:  No evidence of acute cardiopulmonary disease.  Free air below the
hemidiaphragms is consistent with recent surgery.  Nasogastric tube is
somewhat obscured by metallic opacification overlying the upper abdomen,
though the tip appears to be coiled in within the upper fundus of the stomach.
